sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Render runs web services, static sites, private services, background workers, and cron jobs. Web services and static sites are reachable from the public internet. Private services are reachable only over your private network. Background workers run continuously without receiving traffic, and cron jobs run a command on a schedule and then exit.

sections.heading: Limitations
sections.text: A service with an attached disk can't scale to more than one instance, and it doesn't get zero-downtime deploys.

sections.heading: Spin-down behavior
sections.text: A free web service spins down after 15 minutes without inbound traffic. When it receives a request again, Render spins it back up, and the request waits until the service is running. This can take up to a minute.

sections.heading: Free Postgres
sections.text: A free Render Postgres database expires 30 days after it's created. Upgrade it to a paid instance type before then to keep your data.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Render Key Value is a managed, Redis-compatible key-value store. It was previously called Render Redis. Use it for caches, job queues, and session storage.

sections.heading: Port binding
sections.text: Your app must bind to host 0.0.0.0 on the port given in the PORT environment variable. The default value of PORT is 10000.

sections.heading: Web services
sections.text: A web service runs your app and gives it a public onrender.com URL.

sections.heading: Top-level fields
sections.text: The top-level `services` list defines web services, private services, background workers, cron jobs, and Key Value instances. Each service needs a `type` and a `name`. Render Postgres databases are defined in the top-level `databases` list. Environment groups are defined under `envVarGroups`.

sections.heading: Unsupported features
sections.text: Background workers, private services, and cron jobs aren't available on the free instance type. Free web services can't scale beyond one instance.

sections.heading: Zero-downtime deploys
sections.text: By default, Render keeps the old instance serving traffic until the new one is healthy, so web services deploy without downtime. Services with an attached persistent disk are the exception: Render stops the old instance before starting the new one, so there is a short gap.

sections.heading: Deploy for free
sections.text: Render offers free instance types for web services, Render Postgres, and Render Key Value, for hobby projects and testing.

sections.heading: Health checks
sections.text: You can set a health check path. During a deploy, Render waits for this path to return a successful response before routing traffic to the new instance.

sections.heading: File location
sections.text: A Blueprint is defined in a file named render.yaml. By default, Render looks for it at the root of your repository.

sections.heading: Service fields
sections.text: Common service fields include `runtime`, `plan`, `region`, `buildCommand`, `startCommand`, `envVars`, `autoDeploy`, and `healthCheckPath`. A cron job also needs a `schedule`.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: A persistent disk keeps files across deploys and restarts. Disks are available on paid instance types.

sections.heading: Ephemeral filesystem
sections.text: Free instances can't attach a persistent disk. Any file a free service writes at runtime is lost when the service redeploys or spins down.
